sentence: This project builds computational methods that combine data from different sources to understand spatially distributed cells, diseases and drug response.
This project studies how early tau aggregation affects cognition in clinically normal individuals and people with mild cognitive impairment, using imaging and digital biomarkers.
This project provides free access to large databases of physiological and clinical data, and works to streamline and automate how they are run.
This project tries to find out how blocking an enzyme involved in cholesterol synthesis protects against sepsis, using a zebrafish model.
This project studies how brain circuits balance social and primary drives under realistic ecological pressures.
This project develops and tests gene editing approaches for dominant motor neuron diseases, using human induced pluripotent stem cell models of Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 2E.
This project builds an automated microfluidic system that does hands-free library preparation for sequencing from low-input samples.
This project studies how circular, extrachromosomal pieces of DNA form and act in cancer, and looks for ways to target them.
This project studies how cocaine changes spatial patterns of dopamine release in the nucleus accumbens core in response to stimuli.
This project adds genotyping and whole genome sequence data from more individuals to increase the ancestral detail of Alzheimer's disease sample sets.
This project studies what codon biases do to evolution and to how cells work.
This project tries to find out which genes explain why mouse strains differ in how repeated cocaine exposure changes their behavior.
This project develops ways to make recombinant adeno-associated virus for gene therapy that are purer, easier to scale up and more potent.
This project builds a repository of biological interactions to help researchers understand the molecular mechanisms of disease.
This project studies how the transcriptome changes in brain regions and the spinal cord in frontotemporal dementia and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
This project builds an automated tool that uses deep learning on repeated images to predict cancer treatment outcomes early.
This project studies why colorectal cancer that has spread to the liver becomes resistant to an inhibitor of the phosphocreatine transporter.
This project studies how the aryl hydrocarbon receptor in dendritic cells controls the immune response in autoimmune diseases.
This project develops biomarkers from computed tomography images of the legs to find people with spinal cord injury at highest risk of fracture.
